as_written_in_papers.quote: We identified a heterozygous variant in TNFAIP3, namely NM_006290.4:c.460G > T, resulting in a premature stop codon p.(Glu154Ter).
In conclusion, we presented a HA20 patient with gastrointestinal BD-like symptoms and identified a novel heterozygous variant (c.460G > T, p.Glu154Ter) in TNFAIP3.

cases.statement: Three carriers in one Italian paternal lineage: the proband (infant girl, very early-onset colitis and panniculitis), her father (oral aphthosis, vitiligo, thyroiditis) and her father's brother (oral aphthosis, vitiligo).

people.label: patient
people.other_allele: not applicable (also carries a maternally inherited TNFRSF13B c.204dupA risk allele)
people.key_phenotypes: hematochezia from 3 months with active colitis on biopsy; severe anaemia; panniculitis with ulcerative and necrotic skin lesions; fever with high WBC and CRP; arthralgia

quotes.quote: A one-year-old caucasian baby girl came to our attention for severe normocytic anemia, without signs of hemodynamic failure.
From 3 months of age, our patient had a history of hematochezia during exclusive maternal breastfeeding.
The histological examination revealed the presence of active colitis with no signs of chronicity and so the diagnosis of allergic colitis was excluded (Figure 4).
On physical examination baby girl presented ulcerative and necrotic lesions associated with painful edema of the limbs (Figures 5–8).
two months later our patient presented a new relapse with unpainful skin lesions and widespread arthralgia.

quotes.quote: The same TNFAIP3 variant was also found in her father who had suffered from recurrent oral aphthosis, vitiligo and thyroiditis since childhood.

quotes.quote: Later, the father's brother performed genetic test and identified the same mutations in TNFAIP3.
her father's brother with recurrent oral aphthosis and vitiligo

phenotype_specificity.statement: Very early-onset colitis with Behçet-like skin inflammation and a family history on the paternal line. Infection, neoplasm, ADA2 deficiency and VEO-IBD genetic causes were excluded; a custom IUIS gene panel was used. The authors note the colitis presentation and very early onset are rare.

quotes.quote: IFN signature was normal and ADA-2 deficiency was excluded.

Considering the laboratory exams and the early-onset gastrointestinal manifestations, the possibility of very early-onset inflammatory bowel disease (VEO-IBD) was evaluated so blood tests were performed but genetic studies were reported negative (8).
A custom gene panel sequencing including all genes included in the IUIS classification (9, 10) was employed to explore the genetic causes of the clinical phenotype, as previously described (11–13).
Nevertheless, such important symptoms and the very early onset are two rare aspects, not described in other works.

segregation.statement: Two affected relatives carry the variant (father and paternal uncle, both with milder, later-onset disease). The mother was tested and the variant is of paternal origin. Other paternal relatives with possible disease (grandfather with early liver disease, a great-uncle who died at 16, a relative with Crohn's disease) could not be tested.

quotes.quote: Family segregation studies demonstrated the paternal origin of the TNFAIP3 variant and the maternal origin of the TNFRSF13B allele.
Family members truly screened for mutations in TNFAIP3 were the baby girl's mother and father.
The other family members in the paternal line presented potential clinical conditions of HA20 but could not be screened for mutations (Figure 9).

In the family described here, the index patient presented with an infantile onset severe intestinal, joint and skin involvement, while the other affected family members presented later in life, with less severe clinical manifestations.

de_novo.statement: Not de novo in the proband: inherited from her father.

quotes.quote: Family segregation studies demonstrated the paternal origin of the TNFAIP3 variant and the maternal origin of the TNFRSF13B allele.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Nonsense: c.460G>T predicted p.(Glu154Ter). The paper describes HA20 as caused by loss-of-function TNFAIP3 variants.

quotes.quote: It is caused by loss-of-function mutations in TNFAIP3 gene that result in the activation of a pro-inflammatory pathway.

population_data_in_papers.statement: Not present in gnomAD, as stated by the authors.

quotes.quote: This variant was not previously described and is not present in the GnomAD database.

authors_classification.statement: No ACMG class given; the authors established a genetic diagnosis of A20 haploinsufficiency from the variant's characteristics.

quotes.quote: Based on the characteristics of the variant, the genetic diagnosis of A20 haploinsufficiency was established.

concerns: The paper uses NM_006290.4; the batch HGVS is on NM_001270508.2. The protein agrees (protein_check: agrees).
Second variant in the proband: TNFRSF13B NM_012452.3:c.204dupA p.(Leu69ThrfsTer12), maternally inherited, which the authors call a known risk allele and speculate may modify severity.
The paternal uncle's result comes from a later genetic test reported second-hand; the paper writes 'the same mutations' (plural).
Three batch identities (proband, father, uncle) are three different people in one family.
notes_for_panel: One family with three carriers, all with features the authors attribute to HA20; segregation is limited to these relatives and the mother's negative result.
